chapter: Clubs, publishers, unions and life in Denver
title: How bandmates reacted to bad solos; Hawkins' set choruses
summary: Players frowned on a poor performance since you must control your instrument; Hawkins kept fixed choruses like Body and Soul while others fished each night.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: pretty extensively about how the musicians liked to joke around with one another, which is just common. We know that. Did you find them very -- oh, at times vicious with people that couldn't play or something like that? Well, of course, you probably didn't have that much problem with the people, the caliber of people in your band. But suppose some guy came in and really screwed up a chorus or something like that. How did the musicians take that?
You mean -- when you say screwed up, you mean purposely?
No. No, say for some reason or another he really just played a bad chorus or a lot of bluies or whatever, --
-- because of his inability -- or because of his ability, rather, not to be able to play good or what?

Either that or, say, if a musician were, talking some kind of a downer or, you know, having a bad night or something, did the musicians get to him or would they accept that and let it go as being the moment --
Well, the guys wouldn't say anything but (unintelligible) they frowned on that, you know, because they figure you're supposed to perform regardless, you know,

and you're supposed to give a good performance, supposed to have control of your instrument at all times, you know, and this is one of the reasons why Coleman Hawkins had set patterns for certain tunes, you know. You could play a tune three years, and Hawk played a great chorus on that. He would keep that chorus in. This is another thing I liked about him.

He wasn't like the average (unintelligible) guy that -- when you get ready to play a chorus, he don't know what it's going to be. He's searching for it, you know. But Hawk would know where his fingers would lay on this thing. Like "Body and Soul." Hawk would play that, and he'd play it the same way every night. And he would know how it's going to sound, you know, and all this thing. Whereas some of the other tenor players, maybe one night he'd luck up on a great chorus, and the next night he'd stink on the same thing because he's fishing, you know, one of these things.

But, you know, knowing your instrument. You're supposed to play. You're not supposed to make all those blues, you know. If you're not physically able, then you should tell somebody else to take your chorus part, like tonight I don't feel good, you know, one of those things. The guys would know. (Unintelligible).
Now does that answer your question?
Yes. Yes, it does. Thank you.
